## Answers to the three questions

**1. Are the Region C cases linked to the Region A outbreak?**
Probably yes. The Region C genomes belong to TV.2 and its descendants. TV.2 first appears in Region A (1–5 March, S01 on 2 March), and
the first TV.2 case in Region C comes later (OB22, 12 March), only 1 SNP from OB10, an early Region A genome. The large Region C
cluster (TV.2.2, 7 genomes from 25 March) descends from that same ancestor and carries 3 own mutations: it is the result of
**local transmission** in Region C after an introduction. A TV.2.1 genome in Region C (OB14, 2 April) is 4 SNPs from a Region A TV.2.1 genome (OB23) but 10 from the local TV.2.2 cluster: a second link
between the regions, not part of the local cluster. *The tree cannot prove the direction of the introductions*; the dates and the early appearance in Region A make
"A → C" the most plausible reading.

**2. Are the Region B cases part of the outbreak?**
No (not on these data). The Region B genomes are TV.3, 6 SNPs from the root and **without any of the TV.2 mutations**: an older,
independent lineage. Region B and D also have TV.1 background genomes.

**3. How confident, and what next?**
Moderate. Strengths: complete genomes, clear lineage structure, dates that agree with the tree. Limits: very few SNPs
(1–3 per branch), small sample (26 genomes), no contact information, one low-quality genome excluded (OB24, 23 % N).
Next steps: sequence more Region C cases and the cases between 5 and 25 March; collect travel and contact data of OB22 and OB14;
re-sequence the failed samples (S02, S03).

## Example brief (one page)

> **Genomic investigation brief — TOYV1, Regions A–C**  
> **Key message.** The Region C cases are consistent with an introduction from Region A in early March followed by local
> transmission; the older Region B cases belong to a different lineage and are not part of this chain. Confidence: moderate.
>
> **Data and quality.** 28 genomes received (27 outbreak + S01), 27 analysed. OB24 excluded (23 % N). Reference TOYV1.
> Negative control: 50 viral reads (barcode bleed); the samples concerned have > 70x and are not affected.
>
> **Findings.** Lineage TV.2 first seen in Region A on 1–5 March. In Region C: one early TV.2 genome (12 March), a cluster of
> 7 TV.2.2 genomes (25 March–26 April) and one TV.2.1 genome (2 April). Region B: TV.3 (5 genomes) and TV.1, 16 SNPs or more from TV.2.
>
> **Figure.** Tree of 27 genomes coloured by region (maximum-likelihood, 1,000 ultrafast bootstraps).
>
> **Interpretation.** The pattern suggests an introduction followed by local transmission in Region C; the direction of introductions
> is inferred from dates, not demonstrated by the genomes.
>
> **Limits.** Few SNPs (low resolution), small sample, no contact data.
>
> **Recommendations.** Sequence more Region C cases and the March cases; collect travel/contact history for the early Region C and
> TV.2.1 cases; re-sequence samples with insufficient coverage.
